svg.title: Visitor
svg.desc: Visitor. Add new operations to a stable set of classes without editing them: each operation is a visitor that every element accepts. Step 1, Nine edits, mixed concerns: total(), toCsv() and tax() go into every line class: 3 × 3 = 9 edits, and each class mixes concerns. Step 2, Operations as visitors: Each line keeps one method, accept(v); each operation becomes one visitor class, a method per kind. Step 3, Double dispatch: Two hops per line: line.accept(v), then v.visitProduct(this) or its kin; TotalVisitor sums 88.50. Step 4, Add operations, not kinds: TaxVisitor is one new class (EUR 16.80) and no line changes; a new DiscountLine edits every visitor.

g.text: total(), toCsv() and tax() go into every line class: 3 × 3 = 9 edits, and each class mixes concerns.
Each line keeps one method, accept(v); each operation becomes one visitor class, a method per kind.
Two hops per line: line.accept(v), then v.visitProduct(this) or its kin; TotalVisitor sums 88.50.
TaxVisitor is one new class (EUR 16.80) and no line changes; a new DiscountLine edits every visitor.
= 3 operations × 3 line classes, each edited by hand
Every line class now mixes pricing, CSV export and tax rules in one place
The alternative, one function per operation that checks each line's class, repeats the same three checks in every function
Each line class keeps one method, accept(v); each operation becomes one visitor class, with one method per kind
invoice.accept(totalVisitor): each line gets accept(v) and calls the visitor back
Two dispatches: the line’s class picks visitProduct, the visitor’s class picks its code
invoice.accept(csvVisitor): the same accept() calls now run CsvVisitor’s methods
TaxVisitor: one new class, and no line class is edited
Same trade-off: Abstract Factory makes new families cheap and new kinds of product costly
In use: ESLint rules, Babel plugins (by syntax-tree node type), Java’s FileVisitor
Closed set? a TS union with an exhaustive switch, or a Java switch over a sealed type
